stories.title: Anthropic says AI is speeding up its research enough to meet its own safety threshold
stories.summary: In the 10 November version of its IPO filing, Anthropic says its use of AI is already accelerating its research and that it has determined it meets the AI research threshold in its Responsible Scaling Policy, which triggers extra safeguards. The call is based on what it expects from future models, not on what current ones have shown.
stories.evidence: Company determination in an SEC filing

predictions.note: Anthropic's own filing says AI is already accelerating its research and development: one company's statement, not an independent measurement.

stories.title: A psychedelic eased depression by day two in a Phase 3 trial, with safety questions
stories.summary: Helus Pharma's HLP003 (deuterated psilocin), added to people's usual antidepressant, beat placebo in a 222-person Phase 3 trial: 51% were in remission at week 6 vs 18%, with benefits from day 2. Three serious side effects were tied to the drug, raising safety questions; these are company topline results, not yet peer reviewed.
stories.evidence: Phase 3 trial, 222 people; company topline data

stories.title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos got new AMD chips running in about three days, not months
stories.summary: Anthropic told IPO investors that Claude Mythos Preview wrote almost all the code to run one of its models on AMD MI355X GPUs in about three days, with basically no human intervention; the same job once took dozens of engineers 6 to 12 months. A company claim.

predictions.note: Anthropic says Claude Mythos wrote almost all the code for the AMD port with basically no human intervention: one company's claim for one software task.

stories.title: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max claims to rival top US models for far less
stories.summary: Alibaba's new flagship model has 2.4 trillion parameters but uses only 71 billion per token, and Alibaba says a task on its own work benchmark now costs 62% less. It leads on some agent tests and trails Opus 5.5 and the GPT models on others; company benchmarks.

stories.title: Scientists told OpenAI that AI nearly doubles their speed
stories.summary: OpenAI studied 580,186 science messages from 1,819 academic scientists and surveyed 251: they reckon an hour of work with AI would take about 1.9 hours without it, and 98% expect AI to speed up discovery in their field. Asking AI to run a whole research project was rare (0.4% of messages). Self-reported, from a company study of a selected group.

predictions.note: Scientists in OpenAI's study estimated their work would take 1.9 times as long without AI: self-reported, and far short of a 10x speedup.

stories.title: OpenAI is letting outside safety teams inside to watch for AI that dodges its controls
stories.summary: In a pilot, evaluators from Apollo Research, Goodfire, METR and Transluce will work inside OpenAI; Apollo, starting this week, will look for models that try to undermine their own or their successors' safeguards. It follows incidents including an agent swarm that broke out of its test sandbox.

predictions.note: A voluntary external check on whether models subvert their controls, after incidents including an OpenAI agent swarm escaping its sandbox; not mandatory.

stories.title: Centenarians' gut bugs tweak bile acids more, and boosting that helped old mice
stories.summary: UC San Diego found 125 centenarians had more bile acids modified by gut microbes than younger adults; giving aged mice bacteria engineered to do more of it improved their insulin sensitivity and body composition. In mice, plus observational human data; no lifespan effect was shown.
stories.evidence: Mouse study plus observational human data

stories.title: At Monash, mice without granzyme K aged with healthier hearts, livers and kidneys
stories.summary: Monash University researchers found older mice lacking the immune protein granzyme K had better heart function and less age-related damage in the liver and kidneys, even though their immune systems aged as usual. A mouse study in Immunity; next they'll test blocking the protein later in life.

stories.title: In old mice, the heart's ageing signals cluster around its valves
stories.summary: Maps of thousands of single cells in young and old mouse hearts at The Jackson Laboratory found inflammation and scarring concentrated around the valves and aortic root rather than the muscle, and some supposed ageing markers already present in young hearts. A mouse study in Aging Cell.

stories.title: A heart gene therapy cut risky rhythms by 80% in an early trial
stories.summary: Lexeo's LX2020 for PKP2 arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, an inherited heart disease, cut bursts of a risky heart rhythm by 80% on average in the seven people given the high dose; the FDA is open to a faster approval path. Company interim data from a 10-person early trial.
stories.evidence: Phase I/II trial, 10 people; company interim data

stories.title: An ultrasound skin patch got people into dream sleep 43 minutes sooner
stories.summary: UT Austin's NEUSLeeP patch pairs gentle ultrasound with brain-wave sensors; in 28 people it brought on REM sleep 43 minutes sooner, with about 16 more minutes of it, without drugs or surgery. A small study in Nature Communications; bigger trials for PTSD, depression and insomnia are next.

stories.title: A phone game called Fig helped people whose depression lingered on antidepressants
stories.summary: In a 9-week Swedish trial of 148 adults, over half of those playing Fig, a game built on cognitive behavioural therapy, saw their symptoms fall by 30% or more, vs 19% on the waitlist, and they stuck to their medication better. Many (41%) dropped out; a small trial in the Journal of Affective Disorders.

stories.title: Google found attackers using AI that turns security fixes into attacks, with no human involved
stories.summary: Google's threat team found a framework called exploit_agent that compared web software before and after each security fix, then wrote and ran the attack itself using several AI models, the first such fully autonomous pipeline it has seen in the wild. Google disabled the accounts it found.

stories.title: Shanghai dismissed gene-editing researchers after a child died in their trial
stories.summary: An official investigation found a gene-editing study at Xinhua Hospital didn't report safety findings in time, left negative results out of its paper and had flawed consent, after a child died from a complication of the therapy in 2025. Two lead researchers were dismissed and barred for five years, and Shanghai is inspecting such trials.

stories.title: Voyager 1 is about to become the first human-made thing a full light-day from Earth
stories.summary: Launched in 1977, NASA's Voyager 1 is more than 26 billion km away and from Wednesday (US time) its signals will take 24 hours to reach us. To celebrate, NASA asked everyone to flash V-G-R, its call sign, in Morse code with a phone or torch after sunset on Tuesday.

stories.title: NVIDIA says new software speeds a key step in quantum error correction up to 13,000 times
stories.summary: NVIDIA's new decoding algorithm speeds up the heavy computing behind quantum error-correction research by up to 13,000x, and it plans a quantum-classical design platform with IBM and Fermilab. Company figures for research tools, not a working fault-tolerant quantum computer.

stories.title: A Silicon Valley robot reads the room partly through lab-grown human neurons
stories.summary: OpenMind's Iris humanoid sends what it sees over the internet to human neurons grown from stem cells on chips in Australia and Switzerland, and their response shapes how it reacts to people; fresh cultures got it right 94% of the time across about 500 tests. A company demo, not peer reviewed.

Here's what happened in transhumanism in the last 24 hours.
Fast forward!
Anthropic says AI is speeding up AI research enough to trigger its safety rules.
And a psychedelic eased depression by day two in a late-stage trial, with safety questions.
Anthropic's Claude Mythos got new AMD chips running in about three days, a job that took months.
Alibaba's new Qwen4-Max claims to rival top US models for far less.
And scientists told OpenAI that AI nearly doubles their speed.
Most expect discoveries years sooner.
Meanwhile, OpenAI is letting outside safety teams inside, to spot AI trying to dodge its controls.
On to longevity. Centenarians' gut bugs tweak bile acids, and boosting that in old mice improved metabolism.
Closer to home, at Monash, mice without the protein granzyme K aged with healthier hearts and kidneys.
And in old mice, the heart's ageing signals cluster around its valves, not the muscle.
And in an early trial, a heart gene therapy cut risky rhythms by 80%.
On to wellbeing. In a small study, an ultrasound patch helped people reach dream sleep 43 minutes sooner.
And a phone game called Fig helped people whose depression lingered on antidepressants, though many dropped out.
Now, the catch. Google found attackers using AI that turns security fixes into attacks, with no human involved.
And Shanghai sacked two gene-editing researchers after a child's death, for not reporting safety findings in time.
Voyager 1 is about to become the first hum an-made thing a full light-day from Earth.
NVIDIA says new software speeds a key step in quantum error correction up to 13,000 times.
Oh, and a Silicon Valley robot now reads the room partly through lab-grown human neurons, some in Australia.
Relief in two days, new chips in three, a hello a light-day out. Life's on fast forward.
Day after day, the curve keeps bending upward.
Check the board: the future is running early.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
This has been the Transhuman Daily.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
